A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PI-DIONs research. Their complete main text, equations, six figures, seven tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original numerical experiments on reaction-diffusion, Helmholtz and Darcy inverse problems, together with architecture comparisons, sensitivity analyses and irregular-sensor experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains these original numerical experiments and their results in Section 4 and Appendices A–C.

M1.justification: The reconstruction/inverse branches, trunk networks and training losses are unchanged. PI-DIONs-v0 and variable-input PI-DIONs already appear in v1, including their architectural details.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same reaction-diffusion boundary-measurement, Helmholtz internal-measurement and Darcy permeability tasks. Appendix C.3's irregular-sensor scenario is also retained unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains both DeepONet branch configurations and standalone FNO. The PI-DIONs-v0 comparison in Appendix A and PINN comparisons in Appendix C retain the same comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C retain the same sample counts, grids, relative L2 metric, model sizes, loss weights, training procedures and sensor-sampling protocol. The revised theoretical sample bound does not change the reported experimental settings.

E4.justification: The architecture comparison, loss-weight sensitivity analysis, training-sample ablation, PINN timing comparison and irregular-sensor experiment are unchanged in Appendices A and C.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, empirical confidence intervals or significance tests. The delta correction in Theorem 2 concerns a theoretical probability guarantee, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All reported results are retained. For example, Table 1's unsupervised PI-DION errors remain 1.03%, 8.10% and 8.05% for reaction-diffusion, Darcy and Helmholtz, respectively; Appendix C.3 still reports 3.83%. The qualitative result images are identical.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the Helmholtz estimate: the subdomain closures must be disjoint, source-error norms over Ω0 and Ωm replace the whole-domain norm, and an assumed ε-small error in the remaining region accompanies an added ε remainder. Theorem 2 adds division by δ inside both logarithms of its sample-count bound. These are localized revisions to existing guarantees; Appendix D's proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central claims about learning inverse operators without labeled targets, incorporating physical constraints and extending stability estimates to operator learning. No contribution is added or withdrawn.

C2.justification: The Helmholtz discussion now explicitly conditions its estimate on small source error outside the two separated subdomains, adding an applicability qualification. Interpretations of empirical results and discussion of computational limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same architectures, optimizer, learning rate, GPU, batch sizes and data-generation details. Section 6 retains the same statement that source code is submitted as supplementary material.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with physics-informed operator learning, neural inverse operators and variable-input DeepONets. References merely shift across pages.

P1.justification: V2 adds acknowledgments and an ICLR 2025 publication header, locally rewrites the Helmholtz argument, combines discussion paragraphs and clarifies the Table 5 cross-reference. The overall section sequence and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 9 to page 8, Table 1 becomes slightly more compact, and the supervised-loss formula becomes inline. V2 also removes blue text highlighting and adds running publication headers. Figure content and table entries remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical precision by restoring Theorem 2's confidence dependence and making the additional Helmholtz assumptions explicit. Presentation also receives modest cleanup. The benefit is limited because Theorem 3 and Appendix D do not explicitly explain how the new Helmholtz qualification carries through to the global guarantee. The method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
